feedback.problem: Calculate the area of the finite region bounded by the curves $y={x}^{2}-9$ and $y=7.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's draw a sketch of the two functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14013841/assets/85961197a76cc38713537f80a9c97bb158247c71a8be4633c98245ea158634b4.png)

Now, we want to determine the limits of integration. To do this, we equate the two functions and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-9 & =7 \\ {x}^{2} & =16 \\ x & =\pm 4\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we need to integrate from $x=-4$ to $x=4.$

To determine which is the lower function and which is the upper, we draw our vertical arrow.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14013841/assets/7543876e9138be135630313317e162c9b256713f2565b0cd3b5a24bb9ba9a3b3.png)

The vertical line 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y={x}^{2}-9,$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=7.$

Therefore, we can find the area, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{-4}^{4}[\,(\text{upper function})-(\text{lower function})\,]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-4}^{4}[\,(7)-({x}^{2}-9)\,]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-4}^{4}(16-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(16x-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3})|}_{-4}^{4} \\  & =[16\cdot 4-\frac{1}{3}\cdot {4}^{3}]-[16\cdot (-4)-\frac{1}{3}\cdot (-4)^{3}] \\  & =(64-\frac{64}{3})-(-64+\frac{64}{3}) \\  & =\frac{256}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
